source_text:
ὡς "οὐκ

ἔστιν λόγων ἅμα καὶ χρημάτων πλουτεῖν· ὅθεν" φησὶν "ὑπεξείων δὲ τοὺς βότρυς,
ὅπως αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἐπασκήσω τὴν γλῶτταν· ἐπεὶ καὶ οἱ τέττιγες μόνῃ τῇ δρόσῳ
thought_title: Wealth of words and wealth of money cannot coexist
orientation: Procopius is now quoting the imagined speech of Dionysus, who explains why he withheld the grape clusters from the poor man.
pass_a_gloss: As: "It is not possible to be rich in words and in money at the same time; therefore," he says, "I was withdrawing the grape clusters, so that I might cultivate his tongue more; since also the cicadas, fed on dew alone—"

choices.english: to be rich in words and in money at the same time
choices.why: Keeps the parallel structure of the two genitives with πλουτεῖν, preserving the contrast between verbal and monetary wealth.
rejected: to be wealthy in both speech and money
to have riches of both words and money

choices.why: The imperfect tense conveys ongoing or repeated action in the past, matching the explanatory tone of Dionysus's defense.
The verb suggests careful training or exercise, fitting the agricultural metaphor of tending the tongue as one would a plant.
The dative with μόνῃ emphasizes the exclusive source of nourishment, matching the Greek word order and emphasis.

pass_b_english: "It is not possible," he says, "to be rich in words and in money at the same time. Therefore, paradoxical as it seems, I was withdrawing the grape clusters, so that I might cultivate his tongue more. For even the cicadas, feeding on dew alone, hold the Muses within themselves."

last_rejected.why: Brief glosses βότρυς as 'new wine'; 'grape clusters' is not the fixed glossary rendering.
last_rejected.ruling: βότρυς means 'cluster of grapes'; 'grape clusters' is correct, 'new wine' would be wrong.

last_rejected.why: ὑπεξείων is present participle, not imperfect; 'withdrawing' implies ongoing past action, but Greek shows concurrent or general present action.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπεξείων is present participle; 'was withdrawing' renders concurrent aspect adequately within normal range, not a major error.

problems.why: No clear antecedent; reader may think Dionysus or someone else.
problems.fix: Name or clearly identify the poor man earlier.

problems.why: Unclear if 'he' is Dionysus or Procopius; quotation marks help but attribution is muddy.
problems.fix: Clarify 'Dionysus says' at start of speech.

problems.quote: I was withdrawing the grape clusters, so that I might cultivate his tongue more
problems.why: Dionysus as god of wine would not withdraw grapes; paradox needs highlighting.
problems.fix: Add note that this is paradoxical divine economy.

problems.why: Dionysus is called 'the son of Semele' without explanation; a reader may not connect the two.
problems.fix: Add 'Dionysus, the son of Semele,' or gloss 'son of Semele' as Dionysus.

problems.why: The quotation marks signal Dionysus's speech, but the closing quotation mark placement is ambiguous across the section break.
problems.fix: Clarify where Dionysus's speech ends relative to the next section.

edits.new: "It is not possible," Dionysus says, "to be rich in words and in money at the same time.

edits.old: Therefore I was withdrawing the grape clusters, so that I might cultivate his tongue more.
edits.new: Therefore, paradoxical as it seems, I was withdrawing the grape clusters, so that I might cultivate his tongue more.

fixed: The poor man is already identified in the preceding section as the man devoted to the Muses and Graces; no change needed.
Changed 'he says' to 'Dionysus says' to clarify the speaker.
Added 'paradoxical as it seems' to highlight the divine economy.
The work brief names 'the son of Semele' as Dionysus; the English already uses 'Dionysus' consistently.
The quotation marks in the English clearly open and close Dionysus's speech within this section; no change needed.

problems.why: Clear here, but prior section lacks transition into direct speech.
problems.fix: Mark speech beginning explicitly in u01-rem-early.

problems.why: 'The whole Muses' is unidiomatic; reader may think it differs from 'the Muses.'
problems.fix: Use 'the Muses' consistently; 'whole' is a Greek idiom.

problems.quote: Do you want to learn what Dionysus says to all this?
problems.why: Reader may not realize the next section is Dionysus's direct speech until partway through.
problems.fix: Add opening quotation mark before 'It is not possible' or signal the speech.

fixed: The speaker attribution is already clear in the English; the source uses φησὶν, which is rendered as 'he says' in the literal gloss, and the English already identifies Dionysus as the speaker.
The English already uses 'the Muses' consistently; no change is needed.
The English already signals the direct speech with quotation marks and the speaker attribution; no change is needed.
